records.name: The Camden News
records.finding: Published weekly in Camden by Camden News Publishing Co. Charles S. Boyer’s History of the press in Camden County, New Jersey (1921), pages 62–63, reports a first issue on May 8, 1915. The Directory of New Jersey newspapers, 1765–1970 (1977), page 37, gives the same start and leaves the end unknown. It lists Camden County Historical Society holdings dated May 22, June 26 and December 11, 1915, and March 9, 1918. The listed 1918 holding does not establish the final publication year. Boyer’s present-tense description in 1921 suggests possible later activity but does not establish a 1921 issue. The final publication year remains unknown; the title remains inactive. Current custody and the latest surviving issue need confirmation.

sources.description: Charles S. Boyer, History of the press in Camden County, New Jersey (1921), printed pages 62–63. Book pages inspected October 30, 2026; no newspaper masthead inspected.
Wright and Stellhorn, eds., Directory of New Jersey newspapers, 1765–1970 (1977), printed page 37; founding date, unknown end, and holdings. Directory page inspected October 30, 2026.

unresolved: Ask Camden County Historical Society to confirm custody and supply earliest and latest issue mastheads.

records.name: The New Jersey Guardian
records.finding: Published weekly in Newark, Essex County, NJ by the N.J. Guardian Pub. Co. The Library of Congress catalog and the Directory of New Jersey newspapers, 1765–1970 (1977), page 156, give a September 29, 1934 start and an uncertain end, cataloged as ceasing in 1942? The exact final publication year remains unknown; the title remains inactive. The directory says the title became New Jersey Record. The Schomburg Center finding aid Black newspapers—sample issues and additions, collection Sc Micro RS-722, reel 2, lists a December 6, 1941 issue, volume 9, number 14; this is a cataloged holding, not a verified final issue. The 1967 New Jersey Library Association bibliography, page 105, gives conflicting dates: Entry 926 lists 1934–1942, while entry 932 describes a Guardian predecessor in 1933–1943 and a 1943 name change. That conflict does not establish a 1943 Guardian issue, and the founding-year field remains 1934 pending masthead review. Carried the motto 'Voice of the Colored People.' The Library of Congress description is based on Vol. 6, no. 27 (Oct. 28, 1939), not a last issue. The Library of Congress may not hold copies; holdings may exist at other libraries. The latest Guardian and earliest New Jersey Record mastheads are needed to resolve the transition.
